items.text: Night log, rooftop reflector, after the clouds cleared: the first star seemed to drift less after we adjusted the reference mark, but our second check started from a different side of the mount. That changes the comparison. I wrote down which side held the tube and where the counterweight sat, then returned to the original orientation for another ten-minute hold. The trace looked tighter there too. Before we claim the alignment is settled, repeat that original setup on the next clear session with the same eyepiece and a similar target height. Leave the tracking-rate setting as recorded; we have not demonstrated that it caused the earlier drift. The corrected reference-mark offset is on the front of this page, with the old number crossed through. I also sketched the roof edge behind the target because the first observation ended close to that obstruction, and the next observer needs to know why we stopped rather than assuming the equipment failed. The chart clipped to the mount is the version with the large northern labels.

items.text: Seam-ripper note, green linen trousers: the rolled hem looked even on the table, but the left leg sat lower when the neighbour stood in the intended shoes. I had measured over a temporary cuff that folded twice, so the first amount to remove was too large. The corrected figure is on the fitting receipt. Open only enough stitching to flatten the fold, press it gently, and mark the new line with the leg hanging freely before cutting. The right leg has its own pins and should be measured rather than copied automatically. Save the clean offcut in the envelope marked green linen, because the fabric is narrow enough that little usable pieces are easy to lose among the scraps. After basting both hems, ask for a few steps across the room and a seated check; the wrinkle at the knee made the standing front view look shorter than the side view.
